name: Genochondromatosis Type 1

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Multiple Osteochondromas

criteria.description: Presence of two or more osteochondromas (exostoses) arising from the metaphyses of long bones
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in the EXT1 gene
Characteristic radiographic appearance of sessile or pedunculated osteochondromas with continuity of cortex and medulla

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of two or more osteochondromas with typical radiological features, with or without family history or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and radiological criteria are met.

imaging: Radiographs showing multiple sessile or pedunculated osteochondromas with continuity of cortex and medulla
MRI to evaluate cartilage cap thickness and detect malignant transformation
genetic: Pathogenic variants in EXT1 gene (most common)
EXT2 gene mutations less frequently involved
other: Physical examination revealing palpable bony masses near joints
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of both osteochondromas and enchondromas
Similar clinical presentation but milder phenotype
Presence of multiple enchondromas without osteochondromas

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of osteochondroma
New onset of localized pain or neurological symptoms
Cartilage cap thickness greater than 2 cm on imaging
references: Schmale GA, Conrad EU, Raskind WH. The natural history of hereditary multiple exostoses. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 1994;76(7):986-992.
Wuyts W, Van Hul W. Molecular basis of multiple exostoses: mutations in the EXT1 and EXT2 genes. Hum Mutat. 2000;15(3):220-227.
